thread.title: In One Chart: Tech is responsible for nearly all of the market’s 2018 advance—despite Facebook’s stock woes

title: In One Chart: Tech is responsible for nearly all of the market’s 2018 advance—despite Facebook’s stock woes
text:
1:17 p.m. ET Share 
Amazon alone accounts for nearly 37% of the S&P 500’s gain this year Getty Images Ryan Vlastelica Markets reporter 
Technology stocks may have gotten a black eye over the past week, but the U.S. stock market owes a lot to the sector when considering its 2018 move. 
Despite heavy weakness in the sector in recent days—driven in large part by Facebook Inc. FB, -1.75% which has slumped more than 10% over a controversy surrounding its handling of user data —the group’s longer-term outperformance has been a bright spot in the U.S. stock market in 2018. 
How bright? Tech is basically responsible for all of the overall rise in the S&P 500 SPX, -1.46% thus far this year. 
According to Howard Silverblatt, senior index analyst at S&P Dow Jones Indices, the S&P 500 has risen 1.88% on a total-return basis thus far this year, using data that go through the close of trading on Wednesday. By far the top-performing sector over that period has been technology, which has gained 7.52% as one of only five industry groups in positive territory thus far this year. The $SPX YTD 1.88% total return produces fun stats: Information Tech accounts for 94.9% of YTD gain, w/ConsumerStaples -35.6%; $AMZN accounts for 36.6%, $MSFT is next at 12.8%, w/ $AAPL 14th at 2.8%; $PG is worst, w/an -8.0% impact, then $XOM at -7.5%, w/ $FB 9th worst at -4.1% pic.twitter.com/3YPNQxB323 — Howard Silverblatt (@hsilverb) March 22, 2018 
Given the size of tech’s advance, as well as its weight in the index—based on market capitalization, it is the largest S&P 500 sector group by a sizable margin—it has contributed a staggering 94.88% of the overall index’s year-to-date advance. 
Again, this data is through Wednesday’s close; U.S. stocks fell broadly on Thursday , with technology one of the biggest decliners, which will erode the sector’s positive year-to-date contribution. Currently, tech remains up 5.6% for the year. It remains the top-performing sector. 
Among the particular gainers of the sector, Microsoft Corp. stock’s MSFT, -1.83% 8.61% year-to-date rise is responsible for 12.77% of the benchmark index’s gain in 2018, while Nvidia Corp. NVDA, -1.87% (up 28.5%) has contributed 7.64% and Cisco Systems CSCO, -1.57% (16.55%) can take credit for 7.13% of the gain. Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.09% has risen a relatively slight 1.6% thus far this year, but due to its outsize weight in the index—it is the largest company by market value—that translates to 5.11% of the S&P 500’s gain. 
Beyond tech, the consumer-discretionary sector has also pulled more than its weight this year. The sector has gained 6.24% through Wednesday’s close, contributing 38.87% of the overall march higher. 
While tech has been the biggest boost, Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -1.60% counts as the most valuable player of 2018 thus far. The online retailer has jumped 35.26% this year, and it has by itself contributed a staggering 36.63% of the S&P’s gain. In other words, more than a third of the overall market’s gain this year has come from a single, massive company. 
Netflix Inc. NFLX, -2.27% another trading favorite classified as a discretionary stock, has provided the third-biggest boost this year, behind Amazon and Microsoft. The stock’s 64.87% gain easily eclipses Amazon’s, but due to its smaller size, this translates to a contribution of “just” 11.96%. 
The most severe weight on the overall S&P 500 this year have been the consumer-staples sector, where an 8.4% decline is responsible for nearly 36% of the drag against the index. Energy has proved to be another headwind of a sector; it is down 4.32% year-to-date, contributing a negative 12.83% gain to the index. 
On the opposite end of the scale from Amazon, Procter & Gamble PG, -0.16% is the biggest negative contributor this year. It has dropped 15.51%, resulting in an 8% drag in the S&P 500. Exxon Mobil XOM, -1.25% and General Electric GE, -2.16% also stand as major downward pressures thus far this year. Quote References
